title: Alert Intake and Ticket Creation
purpose: Define how alerts, user reports, third-party notices, and automated detections become trackable cases.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Create a consistent intake process so every actionable alert becomes a documented case with enough context for triage.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies to SIEM alerts, EDR alerts, email reports, vulnerability notifications, abuse reports, and partner notifications.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.body: Record the source, timestamp, affected user or asset, alert name, severity, initial evidence, and any automated enrichment. Assign the ticket to the active queue and set the initial status to New.

sections.heading: Required Evidence
sections.body: Include alert screenshots or event IDs, source logs, affected hostnames, usernames, IP addresses, URLs, file hashes, and the reason the event requires analyst review.

title: Phishing Triage
purpose: Provide a repeatable workflow for reviewing suspicious email reports and determining user or environment impact.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Standardize phishing review so analysts capture the same evidence and reach consistent disposition decisions.

sections.heading: Initial Review
sections.body: Inspect sender, recipient, subject, headers, attachments, links, authentication results, and user interaction indicators.

sections.heading: Analysis Steps
sections.body: Review URL reputation, attachment metadata, sandbox results, email gateway verdicts, and any matching messages delivered to other users.

sections.heading: Closure Criteria
sections.body: Document the final verdict, impacted recipients, containment actions, user notifications, and any recommended blocklist or detection updates.

title: Endpoint Malware Investigation
purpose: Guide analysts through endpoint malware validation, scoping, containment, and evidence capture.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Ensure endpoint malware alerts are reviewed with enough context to determine whether containment or escalation is required.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: Review process tree, command line, parent process, file path, signature status, hash reputation, detection name, and endpoint timeline.

sections.heading: Containment
sections.body: If malicious activity is likely, isolate the endpoint according to local authority, preserve evidence, and notify the response lead.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Record detection details, artifacts collected, containment actions, affected users, related hosts, and recommended follow-up.

title: Incident Escalation
purpose: Define when and how an investigation should be escalated from queue work to incident response coordination.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Make escalation decisions consistent and fast when an event meets impact, severity, or uncertainty thresholds.

sections.heading: Escalation Triggers
sections.body: Escalate confirmed compromise, active attacker behavior, sensitive data exposure, privileged account abuse, lateral movement, or unclear high-severity alerts.

sections.heading: Notification
sections.body: Notify the response lead, provide the ticket link, summarize evidence, list affected assets, and identify decisions or approvals needed.

sections.heading: Handoff
sections.body: Include timeline, current status, completed containment, pending actions, known gaps, and recommended next steps.

title: SIEM Alert Triage
purpose: Standardize initial review, enrichment, and disposition of SIEM-generated alerts.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Ensure SIEM alerts are reviewed consistently before closure, escalation, or conversion into an incident.

sections.heading: Review Steps
sections.body: Validate the rule name, severity, entities, timestamps, source indexes, notable fields, and whether the activity matches expected behavior.

sections.heading: Enrichment
sections.body: Add user, host, asset criticality, recent authentication, EDR, vulnerability, and threat intelligence context where available.

sections.heading: Disposition
sections.body: Close benign alerts with rationale, tune noisy detections when appropriate, or escalate alerts with confirmed suspicious activity.

title: Account Compromise Review
purpose: Guide investigation of suspected user account compromise or abnormal authentication activity.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Confirm whether suspicious authentication or account behavior indicates unauthorized access.

sections.heading: Evidence Sources
sections.body: Review identity provider logs, MFA events, mailbox audit logs, VPN sessions, endpoint telemetry, conditional access results, and impossible travel indicators.

sections.heading: Containment
sections.body: If compromise is likely, disable or reset the account according to local process, revoke sessions, preserve evidence, and notify the response lead.

sections.heading: Closure
sections.body: Document affected services, suspicious IPs, timeline, containment actions, and whether additional user or mailbox review is required.

title: Privileged Account Alert
purpose: Define triage steps for suspicious or high-risk privileged account activity.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Prioritize review of administrative account activity because misuse can create broad operational impact.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: Confirm the account role, source system, change performed, business justification, and whether activity aligns to an approved maintenance window.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.body: Escalate unexpected privilege changes, suspicious administrative logons, unusual source locations, or disabled audit controls.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Record the administrative action, affected object, requester or operator, evidence, and final approval or escalation path.

title: Suspicious Network Connection
purpose: Provide a workflow for investigating suspicious outbound or inbound network activity.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Determine whether a network connection is expected business traffic, misconfiguration, scanning, command and control, or attempted intrusion.

sections.heading: Initial Review
sections.body: Review source and destination IPs, ports, protocol, DNS, JA3 or TLS details, proxy logs, firewall action, volume, and frequency.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Identify asset owner, asset criticality, running process, related endpoint alerts, domain age, reputation, and any similar traffic from other hosts.

sections.heading: Action
sections.body: Block or escalate suspicious destinations according to authority, and document scope, evidence, and recommended detection updates.

title: Vulnerability Notification Review
purpose: Normalize review of vulnerability notifications that require security operations tracking.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Ensure vulnerability notifications are assessed for exposure, severity, ownership, and required follow-up.

sections.heading: Triage
sections.body: Capture CVE or advisory ID, affected product, impacted assets, exploitability, internet exposure, available patch, and known active exploitation.

sections.heading: Routing
sections.body: Assign remediation to the owning team and track due dates according to severity and organizational policy.

sections.heading: Closure
sections.body: Close only after remediation evidence, accepted risk, false positive validation, or compensating control approval is documented.

title: Threat Intelligence Indicator Handling
purpose: Define how threat indicators are reviewed, enriched, searched, and converted into detection or blocking actions.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Prevent raw indicators from being used without validation, context, and expiration criteria.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: Check source reliability, indicator type, age, confidence, relationship to active campaigns, and false-positive risk.

sections.heading: Hunting
sections.body: Search SIEM, EDR, proxy, DNS, email, and firewall data for matches within the relevant lookback period.

sections.heading: Action
sections.body: Document findings, add detections or blocks where appropriate, set review dates, and avoid permanent blocks for low-confidence indicators.

title: Incident Communications
purpose: Establish consistent communication expectations during escalated incidents.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Keep responders, leadership, and stakeholders aligned without spreading unverified details.

sections.heading: Cadence
sections.body: Set an update cadence based on severity, active impact, and response tempo. Use concise situation updates with known facts and next actions.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Include summary, impact, timeline, current actions, blockers, decisions needed, and next update time.

sections.heading: Restrictions
sections.body: Do not include sensitive evidence, personal data, or attribution claims unless approved for the audience.

title: Case Closure and Lessons Learned
purpose: Define the minimum requirements for closing cases and capturing improvement opportunities.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Ensure cases are closed with enough detail to support review, reporting, and future detection improvement.

sections.heading: Closure Checklist
sections.body: Confirm final disposition, evidence, timeline, affected assets, containment actions, recovery status, and owner signoff where required.

sections.heading: Lessons Learned
sections.body: Capture detection gaps, process issues, tooling gaps, training needs, and recommended preventive actions.

sections.heading: Follow-Up
sections.body: Create tracked tasks for tuning, documentation updates, control improvements, or additional training.

title: Daily SOC Shift Handoff
purpose: Define what analysts should review, document, and transfer between SOC shifts.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Keep incoming analysts aware of active cases, monitoring gaps, urgent requests, and pending follow-up.

sections.heading: Pre-Handoff Review
sections.body: Review open critical and high cases, escalations, pending approvals, active incidents, detection outages, and watch items.

sections.heading: Handoff Notes
sections.body: Document case IDs, current status, next action, owner, blockers, due times, and any stakeholder expectations.

sections.heading: Completion
sections.body: Confirm the incoming shift acknowledges the handoff and understands immediate priorities.

title: Detection Rule Tuning Request
purpose: Standardize requests to tune noisy, stale, or inaccurate detection logic.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Ensure detection changes are evidence-based and do not weaken useful alert coverage.

sections.heading: Required Details
sections.body: Capture rule name, alert volume, false-positive pattern, affected entities, sample events, recommended condition change, and expected risk.

sections.heading: Review
sections.body: Validate whether tuning should suppress, enrich, threshold, split, or retire the detection.

sections.heading: Post-Change Check
sections.body: Monitor the adjusted rule for volume reduction, missed coverage, and new false-positive patterns.

title: Log Source Health Review
purpose: Guide review of missing, delayed, or malformed security telemetry.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Identify telemetry gaps that may affect alerting, investigations, reporting, or compliance.

sections.heading: Checks
sections.body: Review ingestion status, last event time, parsing errors, sourcetype changes, field extraction issues, and unexpected volume drops.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.body: Determine which detections, dashboards, investigations, or reports depend on the affected source.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.body: Notify the platform owner with evidence, impact summary, affected source, and urgency.

title: Cloud Security Alert Review
purpose: Provide initial triage steps for cloud control plane and workload security alerts.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Review cloud alerts with account, identity, resource, and region context before disposition.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Capture cloud account, subscription or project, region, principal, resource ID, API action, source IP, and service involved.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: Compare the activity to change records, automation roles, deployment pipelines, baseline behavior, and known service accounts.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.body: Escalate unusual privilege use, public exposure, key creation, logging changes, or destructive actions.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure Review
purpose: Define triage for alerts or reports involving possible sensitive data exposure.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Assess suspected exposure while limiting unnecessary access to sensitive content.

sections.heading: Initial Handling
sections.body: Record source, location, data type, suspected audience, exposure duration, owner, and any containment already performed.

sections.heading: Minimization
sections.body: Avoid copying sensitive data into tickets. Use metadata, approved evidence handling, and restricted-access references.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.body: Escalate confirmed or likely exposure to the appropriate privacy, legal, security, or business owner according to policy.

title: Ransomware Indicator Review
purpose: Guide high-priority review of activity that may indicate ransomware preparation or execution.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Accelerate review of destructive or encryption-related activity to support rapid containment.

sections.heading: Indicators
sections.body: Review mass file modification, suspicious archiving, shadow copy deletion, backup tampering, lateral movement, privilege escalation, and unusual remote execution.

sections.heading: Immediate Actions
sections.body: Escalate immediately if multiple indicators align. Preserve evidence and follow approved containment authority.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Record timeline, affected hosts, suspicious commands, user context, observed indicators, and containment actions.

title: Service Outage Security Review
purpose: Define security review steps when a service outage could affect monitoring or incident response.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Understand whether an outage creates security blind spots, response delays, or suspicious operational impact.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.body: Identify affected services, monitoring impact, user impact, start time, known cause, current owner, and expected restoration.

sections.heading: Compensating Monitoring
sections.body: Identify alternate telemetry, manual checks, vendor portals, or temporary watch items until service is restored.

sections.heading: Closeout
sections.body: Document outage duration, missed alerts if known, follow-up tasks, and any required after-action review.

title: Evidence Handling
purpose: Set expectations for collecting, storing, and referencing investigation evidence.

sections.heading: Identify Evidence
sections.body: Determine what evidence is needed for the case, including logs, screenshots, event IDs, files, hashes, URLs, host details, user details, and timestamps.

sections.heading: Capture Context
sections.body: Record the source system, collection time, collector, tool used, query or command, and the reason the evidence supports the investigation.

sections.heading: Store Securely
sections.body: Save evidence only in approved locations and avoid placing sensitive artifacts in broadly visible tickets, notes, or chat channels.

sections.heading: Reference Clearly
sections.body: Reference evidence with approved links, filenames, hashes, event IDs, or case attachments so reviewers can reproduce the finding.

sections.heading: Review Before Closure
sections.body: Before closing the case, confirm the evidence supports the disposition, required artifacts are attached or referenced, and sensitive data is handled correctly.
